focused_validation.scope: Final authority cases plus context privacy, semantic services, prompt provenance, ambient builder and persister

earlier_broad_validation.cause: An existing scope-rotation test reused the exact pre-revocation timestamp as a supposedly new capture
earlier_broad_validation.correction: Assert that the old timestamp is rejected, then advance the capture clock before testing the new conversation scope

counterexamples: A snapshot load returned empty when the authority was closed, conflating unknown state and absent data
A snapshot purge treated closed authority as source revocation and removed the existing file
An unbound preboot capture could receive a new conversation after a restart and bypass the old conversation tombstone
review_after_first_full_suite.correction: Unavailable authority now raises during snapshot validation and preserves files; runtime capture scopes reject unbound captures older than their authority admission start. All three cases run in the final full suite.

proven: main initializes one persistent privacy authority before optional semantic memory and injects the same ledger into NLU, events, context persistence, orchestrator, request router and ambient capture

Disabling semantic memory keeps source revocation and expiry enforcement; a new-process regression rejects Chroma imports while the privacy-only factory initializes and closes correctly without loading preferences
The runtime factory rejects in-memory and unsupported URI paths so disabling recall cannot silently remove durable tombstones
Optional semantic memory borrows the actual ledger and capture scopes; closing it does not close the authority or release the shared writer lease
Privacy I/O has two dedicated executor threads and eight retained work slots; a saturated one-thread semantic/default executor does not starve privacy revocation
Native borrower completion is retained after close observation timeout; a competing writer remains denied until native work actually exits and the authority finishes cleanup
Cancelled initialization keeps its cleanup registration, actual native work, executor and writer ownership until completion

Raw source and semantic receipts fail closed after ledger shutdown; event and snapshot reads/purge distinguish unavailable authority from committed revocation and preserve unknown-state persistent data
Capture validation precedes scope mutation; revocation timestamp fences survive in-process rotation and unbound preboot captures cannot invent a fresh conversation after restart
Both voice modes reject revoked captures before processing while fresh conversation and explicitly authorized local climate control still function with semantic memory disabled
Ambient capture provenance is fixed before awaiting STT; a revoked or closing source is discarded before tagger invocation when STT returns

Authority-backed ambient stores require a preassigned conversation, reject late reinsertion and attachment, honor the earlier input deadline and revalidate text after async SQL reads and audio after file I/O
Revoked FLAC paths are durably queued before row removal; failed unlink remains pending across store/privacy restart and succeeds on retry
Ambient debug metadata no longer copies transcript previews or speaker names
The source-free CPython 3.13 runtime exercises the shared owner and a privacy-only disabled-memory graph outside the source checkout

ownership.semantic_native_workers: Remain in the optional memory scope; the shared authority waits their actual closing task without sharing their executor
ownership.borrower_registration: Weak bound-method registrations avoid retaining private caches after the semantic owner is unused
ownership.writer_order: Lease acquisition precedes schema initialization/migration; lease release follows actual borrowers, privacy work and executor shutdown
